unit_attributes.statement: The role of the consular officer is limited to providing information obtained from foreign officials on requirements for local marriages and performing notarial and authentication services.

Prior to November 9, 1989, consular officers, when requested to do so, could make certain that foreign marriages were effective for purposes of U.S. law by acting as official witnesses to the marriage when one of the contracting parties was a U.S. citizen, pursuant to the authority of Section 31 of the Act of June 22, 1860 (12 Stat. 79; 22 U.S.C. 4192), which also provided for issuance of an official certificate of witness to such marriage.
unit_attributes.scope_text: Prior to November 9, 1989, when requested to do so, and when one of the contracting parties was a U.S. citizen
references: Section 31 of the Act of June 22, 1860

unit_attributes.statement: Section 31 was repealed, effective February 16, 1990, by Section 123 of the FY 1990-1991 Foreign Affairs Authorization Act.
references: Section 123 of the FY 1990-1991 Foreign Affairs Authorization Act

unit_attributes.statement: Certificates of Witness to Marriage, issued by consular officers pursuant to Section 31 of the Act of June 22, 1860, prior to its repeal, remain valid; such certificates, using the most recent edition of Form FS-87, were issued from when it was revised in October 1939 until November 9, 1989.
references: Section 31 of the Act of June 22, 1860

unit_attributes.statement: Diplomatic and Consular officers and U.S. Ambassadors cannot conduct marriage ceremonies.
unit_attributes.actor: Diplomatic and Consular officers and U.S. Ambassadors
unit_attributes.actor_quote: Diplomatic and Consular officers and U.S. Ambassadors

unit_attributes.statement: You cannot issue any official certificate with respect to marriage laws, even if knowledgeable about the laws of marriage of the receiving state (22 CFR 92.4(a)).
unit_attributes.scope_text: even if knowledgeable about the laws of marriage of the receiving state

unit_attributes.statement: You cannot make any official certification about the status or eligibility to marry of persons residing in the United States who propose to be married abroad, or about the laws of the United States or of any of the fifty States or Territories about eligibility for marriage or the solemnization of a marriage.
You cannot give an official or authoritative opinion on matters of local (receiving state) law and practices to parties proposing to be married abroad.
